title: AC's literal '100 ms' motion-strip evidence is unmet; a 60 Hz substitution is used instead
evidence:
**Acceptance wording (Perkins r1 N13):** the AC's literal "100 ms" strip is
tick-aligned (100 ms = 2 ticks), so a 100 ms cadence samples only tick
boundaries and steps identically before/after — it cannot show the glide.
The decisive evidence is the **60 Hz (17 ms) cadence** substitution below
(3 sub-tick samples per tick): before holds ~3 frames then jumps, after
moves every frame.
detail: The AC demands "motion strip captures at 100 ms show continuous progression, no 50 ms jumps", but 100 ms sampling aliases the 20 Hz tick grid, so the specified evidence cannot show the fix; only the substituted 60 Hz table does.
recommended_fix: Ratify the documented 60 Hz substitution explicitly (amend the AC wording or note the deviation in the PR), keeping the 100 ms strips as supplementary visual-only artifacts.

title: `snapshot` strip mode is claimed 'the PRE-2.1 render, byte-identical' but still applies the +15% packet radius
detail: Snapshot strips render at the current sha with PACKET_R_FACTOR applied, so they are byte-identical to today's golden path — not to actual pre-2.1 pixels. Only interpolation is isolated; the centroid measurement is unaffected.
recommended_fix: Reword the motion_strip.odin comment and PR-body claim to 'the current golden-path snapshot render (includes the +15% size)', noting before-strips differ from true pre-2.1 by packet radius.
